big_case.notes: Routine federal-employee FTCA/FECA primary-jurisdiction dispute arising from an unpublished motions-panel summary affirmance after the petitioner declined to file a FECA claim during a district-court stay, with the Government waiving its response and the Court denying certiorari without comment on the first conference order list.

leakage.notes: Forward-mode prediction run on 2026-10-31 against the 2026-10-31 snapshot, nine days before the 2026-11-09 denial order. External CourtListener and web queries targeted only the 2003 and 2020 circuit precedents cited in the petition (Moe v. United States and Fuqua v. USPS).

central_claims.basis: outcome.json records actual_disposition='denied', actual_granted=0, resolved_at='2026-11-09', and signals.distribution_count=1.
central_claims.claim: The Court will deny the petition without a separate writing following its first conference on November 6, 2026, with zero additional distributions.
The Court will not invite the Solicitor General's views (CVSG) because the United States is already a respondent and has waived a response.
No Justice will write a noted dissent or statement respecting the denial of certiorari.

central_claims.basis: Certiorari was denied, so conditional grant and route predictions were not tested by the outcome.
central_claims.claim: Conditional on granting review, the Court would narrow the question to whether a federal court must refer an arguably work-related emotional-injury claim to the Department of Labor before entertaining an FTCA action, and decide it after plenary briefing and argument rather than summary disposition.
